title: Fix batch_size_effective mismatch: compute post-admission-control + add regression tests
author: Omar El-Sayed
description:
Context: SCM and downstream attribution use `batch_size_effective` to explain batch efficiency (and to reconcile estimated vs metered cost). We found a mismatch where `batch_size_effective` was computed at batch formation time (pre-admission control), but the request set can be reduced by admission control (tenant quotas / concurrency caps / shed). That caused `batch_size_effective` to be inflated for some routes/tenants, leading to (a) optimistic batch-efficiency attribution in the explain endpoint and (b) drift in the mismatch detector when comparing SCM estimates vs metered attribution.

Fix: move `batch_size_effective` computation to the post-admission step, using the admitted request count for the batch (and explicitly recording a separate `batch_size_pre_admission` for debugging only; not exported to SCM dims).

Also adds regression tests that simulate admission control dropping requests from a batch and assert that emitted `batch_size_effective` equals the admitted count, not the pre-admission batch size. Includes a golden metric payload snapshot for the runtime->telemetry event.

Why this is safe: This is a semantics correction for a signal that is already versioned/defined as "effective batch size". No API surface changes. Existing dashboards will shift for affected tenants/routes; this should reduce explain mismatches and remove false positives in drift alerts.

Rollout/notes: Guarded behind existing runtime metrics flag `runtime.telemetry.emit_batch_signals` (default on in staging, on in prod). No additional counters added; overhead unchanged.

Test plan: unit tests for admission control path; integration test via `runtime_metrics_emission_test` in CI; verified locally that mismatch detector no longer flags the synthetic canary prompt set (see internal note in ENG-23217).

Screenshots/logs: attached in internal build (not included here) showing before/after metric payload with admission control dropping 3/16 requests.

Follow-ups: After this lands, we should backfill/update the internal runbook text for "batch efficiency" tooltips to clarify that it uses admitted batch size (Console copy already says "effective").
commits: runtime/metrics: compute batch_size_effective after admission control (use admitted_count)
runtime/telemetry: stop exporting pre-admission batch size as batch_size_effective
tests: add regression coverage for admission-control drop scenario
illustrative_diff_snippet: Before (bug): batch_size_effective = len(batch.requests) computed prior to admission control. After (fix): batch_size_effective = admitted_count, computed immediately after admission decision and before telemetry emission. A non-exported debug field batch_size_pre_admission is retained for logs only.
review_conversation: Sofia Ivanova: Can you confirm this doesn’t change how we compute continuous batching occupancy? I only want to change the SCM signal, not scheduling behavior.

Omar El-Sayed (author): Yep—no scheduling behavior change. This is strictly the metric computation point + which count we use for emitted signal. Scheduler still forms the same batch; admission control still drops the same requests when needed.

Jordan Lee: Please make sure we don’t introduce a new dimension or rename anything that would break determinism/compat tests. Also, can we add an explicit test that fails if batch_size_effective > admitted_count?

Omar El-Sayed (author): Added `TestBatchSizeEffective_EqualsAdmittedCount_WhenAdmissionDropsRequests` and an assertion that effective <= pre-admission always. No schema changes; same field name, corrected semantics.
Logan Wright: Telemetry side: are we changing tags/series cardinality? Also, golden payload snapshot should omit tenant ids etc.
Omar El-Sayed (author): No new tags; same series. Golden snapshot uses anonymized route/model and a fake tenant hash; nothing customer-identifying.
Nadia Rahman: This should fix the metered vs estimate mismatch we saw in canary. Can you link the mismatch detector query you used so we can validate after merge?
Omar El-Sayed (author): Linked internal query in ENG-23217 comment; also added a note in the PR description re: canary prompt set.
Sofia Ivanova: Approved once tests are green.
Jordan Lee: Approved. Thanks for tightening the semantics; this was a confusing one.
